newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Government troops killed, wounded in Tajik clashes.
newsitem.headline: Government troops killed, wounded in Tajik clashes.

text.p: Four government soldiers were killed and 14 wounded in clashes with opposition fighters in Garm, some 150 km (100 miles) east of the Tajik capital, Russia's Interfax news agency said on Friday.

The fighting makes a mockery of a ceasefire supposed to have begun at midnight on Wednesday. Interfax, citing "well-informed sources" inside Tajikistan's interior ministry, said clashes were still raging in the town.
It said rebel forces had surrounded a battalion of Tajik interior ministry troops near Garm where fighting has continued on and off for several days.

The agency said the guerrillas were hammering the battalion with anti-aircraft guns, automatic weapons and rocket-propelled grenades. It said the fighters had also sustained casualties but gave no further details.
The government of the former Soviet republic on Thursday issued a note of protest to the United Nations, accusing opposition forces of violating the ceasefire.
Nerves were also on edge in Dushanbe where two bombs killed one person and injured another on Thursday. It was not clear who planted the devices.

Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed a ceasefire from midnight on Wednesday following peace talks in northern Afghanistan. They are due to sign some form of peace accord in Moscow next week.

Ceasefires declared during the former Soviet republic's bitter four-year civil war have been routinely flouted. A U.N.-sponsored ceasefire reconfirmed in July collapsed almost as soon as it was signed.
